# Zynkbot on Android: how the build is put together

This is a description of the Android build as it exists in the source on the `memory` branch, written for a developer who has to change it. It is not a user guide. Paths under `zynkbot_rust/src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/ai/containai/zynkbot/` are written below as just the Kotlin file name. Rust paths are relative to `zynkbot_rust/src-tauri/src/`.

The short version: the app is a Tauri 2 WebView app (`ai.containai.zynkbot`) whose Rust core is compiled into `libapp_lib.so`. The Kotlin layer around it is unusually large for a Tauri app because the hands-free voice pipeline (wake word, dictation, spoken reply) runs entirely in native code without the WebView, and reaches the Rust core through a JNI function rather than through Tauri.

## 1. Layout: what lives where on the phone

All Rust-side state lives under the app-private files directory. `db::get_app_data_dir()` (`db.rs`) has an Android branch: it takes `$HOME` (which the comment says is the app data directory, falling back to `/data/data/ai.containai.zynkbot`) and appends `files/zynkbot`. Kotlin's `context.filesDir` is `/data/data/ai.containai.zynkbot/files`, so the two sides agree on the tree:

| Path (under `/data/data/ai.containai.zynkbot/files/`) | Written by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `zynkbot/zynkbot.db` | `db::get_db_path` | SQLite database; migrations in `src-tauri/migrations/` |
| `zynkbot/.env` | `commands/models.rs` (`set_api_key`, `set_preferred_backend`), `zynksync.rs`; loaded by `dotenv` in `lib.rs run()` | API keys, `ZYNK_MODEL_BACKEND`, pushed sync settings. Read-only from Kotlin via `EnvFile.kt` |
| `zynkbot/.zynk_user_id`, `.zynk_device_id`, `.zynk_device_name`, `.zynk_current_session`, `.zynk_user_info.txt` | `user_identity.rs` `IdentityManager` (Android branch uses `get_app_data_dir()`; desktop uses `dirs::config_dir()/Zynkbot`) | User and device identity; the thread the app last showed |
| `zynkbot/backup.key`, `zynkbot/backup_key_acknowledged` | `commands/backup.rs` `key_path`, `key_acknowledged_path` | R2 backup encryption key and the "I saved it" flag |
| `zynkbot/user_profile.json` | `db::get_user_profile_path` | user profile |
| `zynkbot/knowledge_base/<user_id>/` | Rust `kb_rag::get_kb_folder_path`; Kotlin `ZynkbotPathsBridge.copyToKnowledgeBase` writes to the same folder | Knowledge Base documents the Rust scanner indexes |
| `zynkbot/wake_triggers/` | `WakeWordService.saveTriggerClip`, `labelLastClip` | Wake-word trigger clips and labels (section 7) |
| `zynkbot/models/system`, `zynkbot/models/user` | created in `lib.rs run().setup` | model directories (no local LLM on Android, see section 11) |
| `vosk-model/` | `MainActivity.extractVoskModelIfNeeded` (copied from APK assets) | Vosk speech model. Note: directly under `files/`, not under `zynkbot/` |
| `wake-word-models/` | `WakeWordBridge.extractModelsFromAssets` | the three ONNX wake-word models. Also directly under `files/` |

Two SharedPreferences files hold Kotlin-only state: `zynkbot_voice` (key `input_source`, section 8) and `zynkbot_setup` (key `asked_assistant_role`, section 4).

The one public location is `Downloads/ZynkbotShare/` (`/storage/emulated/0/Download/ZynkbotShare/`), created by `MainActivity.zynkShareDir()` via `Environment.getExternalStoragePublicDirectory(DIRECTORY_DOWNLOADS)`. The page registers it as the device's single ZynkLink share (`ZynkLinkPanel.jsx` calls `AndroidPaths.getShareDir()` and then the `share_directory` command with `shareName: 'ZynkbotShare'`).

Why the split: ZynkbotShare is the folder the user is meant to open in the phone's Files app (`ZynkbotPathsBridge.openShareFolder`) and receive ZynkLink files into, so it has to be a public folder; an app may create and read its own files there without any storage permission. The Knowledge Base stays app-private because the Rust scanner reads it with plain `std::fs`, and reading files another app put in a public folder would need `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, which Google Play does not grant to an app like this (KI-015 in `docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`). So both folders are fed by copying: `pickFile` copies a picked file into ZynkbotShare, `copyToKnowledgeBase` copies into the KB folder, and files other apps drop into ZynkbotShare are invisible to the app by design.

## 2. The generated-but-hand-edited Android project

`tauri android init` generates `src-tauri/gen/android/`. In this repository the directory is committed and hand-edited, and re-running `tauri android init` would overwrite the hand-written files with Tauri's defaults. `zynkbot_rust/CLAUDE.md` states the rule; its file list was brought in line with this table on 2026-09-09.

Hand-written and tracked in git (line counts from `wc -l` on 2026-09-09):

| File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `MainActivity.kt` | 1087 | Activity, permission queue, model unpacking, all six JavaScript bridges |
| `WakeWordService.kt` | 968 | Foreground service: ONNX wake-word loop, clips, back-off, hand-off |
| `ZynkAssistantSession.kt` | 522 | One assistant invocation: Z overlay, dictation, answer |
| `NativeVoiceAnswerer.kt` | 408 | JNI call into Rust, streaming text-to-speech, pending turns |

| `VoiceCommands.kt` | 158 | Timer, alarm, stopwatch parsing and clock-app intents |
| `ZynkAssistantService.kt` | 68 | `VoiceInteractionService` (assistant role) |
| `SyncForegroundService.kt` | 59 | `dataSync` foreground service |
| `ZynkCore.kt` | 57 | JNI declaration for `nativeSendMessage` |
| `WakeVerifier.kt` | 52 | Personal logistic-regression verifier over embeddings |
| `EnvFile.kt` | 31 | Read `files/zynkbot/.env` from Kotlin |
| `ZynkRecognitionService.kt` | 29 | Stub `RecognitionService` required by the assistant role |
| `ZynkAssistantSessionService.kt` | 14 | Creates a `ZynkAssistantSession` per invocation |
| Total Kotlin | 3694 | |

Also hand-edited and tracked: `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `app/build.gradle.kts` (dependencies, SDK levels, signing), `app/src/main/res/xml/voice_interaction_service.xml`, `app/src/main/res/raw/wake_chime.wav` and `wake_chime_close.wav`, and `app/src/main/assets/` (the Vosk model, 68 MB on disk, and `wake-word-models/` with `melspectrogram.onnx`, `embedding_model.onnx`, `hey_zynk.onnx`, `hey_zynk_verifier.json` and `ATTRIBUTION.txt`, 3.2 MB). `buildSrc/` (Tauri's Gradle `RustPlugin` and `BuildTask`) is tracked unmodified.

Generated by the Tauri CLI at build time and gitignored (`gen/android/.gitignore`, `app/.gitignore`): `app/tauri.properties` (versionName/versionCode), `app/tauri.build.gradle.kts`, `tauri.settings.gradle` (absolute paths into `~/.cargo/registry`), `app/src/main/assets/tauri.conf.json`, `app/proguard-tauri.pro`, `app/src/main/java/ai/containai/zynkbot/generated/*.kt` (`WryActivity`, `TauriActivity`, `RustWebView`, `Rust.kt`, etc.), and `jniLibs/**/*.so`. `keystore.properties` is gitignored; `keystore.properties.template` is tracked.

## 3. Manifest

Permissions declared in `AndroidManifest.xml` and what uses them:

| Permission | Used by |
|---|---|
| `INTERNET` | LLM API calls and the ZynkSync/ZynkLink HTTP server in Rust; `OpenAiDictation.transcribe`; the download fallbacks in `VoskBridge.downloadModel` and `WakeWordBridge.downloadModels` |
| `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC` | `SyncForegroundService` (`FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC`) |
| `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE` | `WakeWordService` (`FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MICROPHONE` on Android 14+) |
| `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` | the two service notifications and the transcript fallback notification; requested at runtime on 13+ by `requestNotificationPermissionIfNeeded` |
| `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` (maxSdkVersion 32) | requested only by `FolderPickerBridge.pick` on SDK <= 32 |
| `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` (maxSdkVersion 29) | requested in `onCreate` on SDK <= 28 before `ensureShareDir()` |
| `CAMERA` | `AndroidCameraBridge.takePicture` |
| `RECORD_AUDIO` | every microphone reader: `WakeWordService`, `VoskBridge`, the session's Vosk, `OpenAiDictation` |
| `MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS` | declared; no direct use found in the Kotlin sources kept for now because vosk-android's `SpeechService` or the WebView's `getUserMedia` may rely on it; a removal candidate after the beta |
| `com.android.alarm.permission.SET_ALARM` | `VoiceCommands.execute` and `VoiceCommandBridge` (AlarmClock intents) |
| `WAKE_LOCK` | `WakeWordService` partial wake locks; `ZynkAssistantSession.wakeScreen` |

`MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT` and `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` were removed on 2026-09-07 for Google Play and must not come back (CLAUDE.md, ROADMAP items 3, 5, 6).

Services: `.SyncForegroundService` (`foregroundServiceType="dataSync"`, not exported) and `.WakeWordService` (`foregroundServiceType="microphone"`, not exported) are the two foreground services. The assistant role needs three exported services: `.ZynkAssistantService` (permission `BIND_VOICE_INTERACTION`, intent filter `android.service.voice.VoiceInteractionService`, meta-data `android.voice_interaction` pointing at `@xml/voice_interaction_service`), `.ZynkAssistantSessionService` (same permission), and `.ZynkRecognitionService` (permission `BIND_RECOGNITION_SERVICE`, intent filter `android.speech.RecognitionService`). The XML declares `sessionService`, `recognitionService`, `supportsAssist="true"` and `supportsLaunchVoiceAssistFromKeyguard="true"`. The recognition service is a stub that answers `ERROR_CLIENT`; it exists only because the framework's `VoiceInteractionServiceInfo` parser rejects an assistant without one (comment in `ZynkRecognitionService.kt`).

A `FileProvider` (`${applicationId}.fileprovider`, paths in `@xml/file_paths`) serves the camera output file. `MainActivity` is `launchMode="singleTask"`, exported, with `MAIN`/`LAUNCHER` and `LEANBACK_LAUNCHER`.

The `<queries>` block declares intents rather than package names so the app can resolve and bind on Android 11+: browser (`VIEW` http/https), `TTS_SERVICE` and `RecognitionService` (the Pixel fix: without the TTS entry the engine resolved as blocked and TTS init failed), the clock actions (`SET_TIMER`, `SET_ALARM`, `SHOW_TIMERS`, `SHOW_ALARMS`, `DISMISS_ALARM`, `SNOOZE_ALARM`), `DIAL` tel, `SENDTO` smsto/mailto, calendar `INSERT`, `VIEW` geo and google.navigation, `WEB_SEARCH`, `MEDIA_PLAY_FROM_SEARCH`, `IMAGE_CAPTURE`, and `SEND` `*/*`.

## 4. Startup sequence in MainActivity

`MainActivity.onCreate` runs, in order:

1. `enableEdgeToEdge()`, then `super.onCreate`. The content view gets a fixed background (`0xFF181A20`) and an insets listener that pads for status bar, gesture bar and cutout, because the WebView cannot pad for them itself (comment in code, targetSdk 36 makes edge-to-edge mandatory).
2. `setShowWhenLocked(true)` and `setTurnScreenOn(true)` (or the legacy window flags below API 27).
3. On SDK <= 28 without `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`: request it (`REQ_WRITE_STORAGE`), and create ZynkbotShare in the result callback. Otherwise `ensureShareDir()` now.
4. The permission queue (`permissionQueue`, an `ArrayDeque` of lambdas) is filled in this order: `requestRecordAudioIfNeeded`, `requestNotificationPermissionIfNeeded`, `requestAssistantRoleIfNeeded`, `requestLocalNetworkPermissionIfNeeded`. `runNextPermissionRequest()` pops one. Each step either shows a dialog and returns, or calls `runNextPermissionRequest()` itself when nothing is needed. `onRequestPermissionsResult` advances the queue for `REQ_RECORD_AUDIO`, `REQ_NOTIFICATIONS` and `REQ_LOCAL_NETWORK`; the assistant-role step advances from its `registerForActivityResult` callback. One at a time because Android shows one permission dialog per Activity at once and the code comment records that firing all together silently dropped the microphone request. Microphone is first because the wake word needs it.
5. `extractVoskModelIfNeeded()`: if `files/vosk-model` is missing or empty, copy `assets/vosk-model` recursively (`copyAssetDir`) on a background thread.
6. `startSyncService()`: `startForegroundService` for `SyncForegroundService`.

The assistant-role prompt (`requestAssistantRoleIfNeeded`) runs once per install: on Android 10+, if `zynkbot_setup/asked_assistant_role` is false, `RoleManager.isRoleAvailable(ROLE_ASSISTANT)` and the role is not held, it sets the flag and launches `createRequestRoleIntent(ROLE_ASSISTANT)`. Holding the role is what lets `WakeWordService` open an assistant session (section 6).

The local-network step exists because Android 16 (SDK 36) makes LAN access a runtime permission (`android.permission.ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK`, spelled as a string literal because older SDK stubs lack the constant); without an explicit request, ZynkSync pairing on 192.168.x.x was blocked.

The wake-word ONNX models are not unpacked in `onCreate`. `WakeWordBridge.isModelReady()` copies any missing file from `assets/wake-word-models/` to `files/wake-word-models/` on demand (ONNX Runtime needs a real file path), and `downloadModels()` does the same with a GitHub-release download as a last resort.

Bridges are registered in `onWebViewCreate(webView)`, which the generated `WryActivity.setWebView` calls once the Tauri WebView exists. `WakeWordService` is not started here; the page starts it (section 5).

`onNewIntent` and `onResume` handle the `wake_word_transcript` extra: a transcript delivered by the native fallback path is held in `pendingWakeTranscript` and pushed to `window.__handleScreenOffTranscript` 800 ms after resume, because `evaluateJavascript` on a paused WebView is silently dropped. `onResume` also calls `ZynkAssistantSession.current?.hideOverlay()` so the Z overlay does not sit over the app.

## 5. The bridges (JavascriptInterface objects)

Registered with `webView.addJavascriptInterface(...)` in `MainActivity.onWebViewCreate`. Results go back to the page by `evaluateJavascript` calling `window.__*` callbacks the page installs beforehand.

**`AndroidFolderPicker`** (`FolderPickerBridge`)
- `pick()`: request legacy storage permission if SDK <= 32, then `OpenDocumentTree`; resolves `window.__fpResolve(path)` / `__fpReject`.

**`AndroidPaths`** (`ZynkbotPathsBridge`)
- `setVoiceInputSource(src)`: store `'vosk'` or `'openai'` in SharedPreferences `zynkbot_voice/input_source`.
- `getShareDir()`: absolute path of `Downloads/ZynkbotShare`, created if missing.
- `pickFile()`: `OpenDocument`, copies the file into ZynkbotShare on a thread; `__zfpResolve(path)` / `__zfpReject`.
- `pickImages()`: `PickMultipleVisualMedia(20)`, image only; `__pickFilesResolve([uri...])` / `__pickFilesReject`.
- `pickDocuments()`: `OpenMultipleDocuments("*/*")`; same callbacks.
- `readFileBase64(uri)`: read a `content://` URI through `ContentResolver`, base64, no wrap.
- `readFileText(uri)`: read a `content://` URI as UTF-8 text.
- `getFileName(uri)`: `DISPLAY_NAME` from the resolver, else the last path segment.
- `copyToKnowledgeBase(uri, userId)`: copy into `files/zynkbot/knowledge_base/<userId>/`, never overwriting (`name (2).ext`); returns the new path or `""`.
- `openUrl(url)`: `ACTION_VIEW` for http/https only (Report a problem opens GitHub issues).
- `getDeviceInfo()`: manufacturer, model, Android version, SDK.
- `openShareFolder()`: opens ZynkbotShare via the Downloads document provider, then the external-storage provider, then a file manager app.

**`AndroidCamera`** (`AndroidCameraBridge`)
- `takePicture()`: request `CAMERA` if needed, then `TakePicture` into a cache temp file through the FileProvider; `__camResolve(path)` / `__camReject`.

**`VoskBridge`** (in-app mic button)
- `isModelReady()`: `files/vosk-model` exists.
- `getModelDir()`: its path.
- `startListening()`: request `RECORD_AUDIO` if missing; load `org.vosk.Model` once, publish it as `WakeWordService.sharedVoskModel`, start a `SpeechService` at 16 kHz; fires `__voskStarted`, `__voskPartial(text)`, `__voskResult(text)`, `__voskError(msg)`.
- `stopListening()`: stop the `SpeechService`; the final result arrives through `__voskResult`.
- `downloadModel()`: download `vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15.zip` from alphacephei.com into `files/vosk-model`; `__voskDownloadProgress(n)`, `__voskModelReady`, `__voskDownloadError`.

**`WakeWordBridge`**
- `isModelReady()`: the three ONNX files present, extracting from assets if not.
- `start(threshold)`: refuse without `RECORD_AUDIO` (`__wakeWordError`); wire `NativeVoiceAnswerer.onSpeakingChanged` to `__nativeSpeaking(bool)` and `onTurnCompleted` to `__nativeTurns()`; `startForegroundService(WakeWordService)` with extras `threshold` and `modelDir`.
- `stop()`: `stopService(WakeWordService)`.
- `stopSpeaking()`: `NativeVoiceAnswerer.stopSpeaking()` (the in-app Stop button).
- `isNativeSpeaking()`: `NativeVoiceAnswerer.speaking`.
- `drainNativeTurns()`: JSON array of finished hands-free exchanges, cleared on return.
- `log(message)`: `Log.i("ZynkWeb", ...)`, breadcrumbs from the page into logcat.
- `downloadModels()`: extract from assets, else fetch from the `wake-word-models` GitHub release; `__wakeWordDownloadProgress`, `__wakeWordModelReady`, `__wakeWordDownloadError`.

**`VoiceCommandBridge`** (in-app typed or dictated commands, `App.jsx handleSendMessage` via `parseVoiceCommand`)
- `setTimer(seconds)`, `setAlarm(hour, minute, label)`: AlarmClock intents with `EXTRA_SKIP_UI=false` (the clock UI is shown, unlike the hands-free path).
- `startStopwatch()`: `android.intent.action.START_STOPWATCH`, else launch a clock app.

Web-side users: `useVoiceInput.js` (`VoskBridge`, and `isAndroid = !!window.VoskBridge`), `useVoiceSession.js` (`WakeWordBridge`, `AndroidPaths.setVoiceInputSource`, `VoiceCommandBridge`), `App.jsx` (`AndroidPaths` pickers and readers, `AndroidCamera`, `WakeWordBridge.drainNativeTurns`, `WakeWordBridge.log`), `ZynkLinkPanel.jsx` and `ZynkFileBrowserModal.jsx` (`getShareDir`, `pickFile`, `openShareFolder`), `KnowledgeBaseManager.jsx` (`pickDocuments`, `copyToKnowledgeBase`), `ReportProblemModal.jsx` (`getDeviceInfo`, `openUrl`).

## 6. The hands-free pipeline end to end

**Starting the listener.** `useVoiceSession.js` is the only place that calls `WakeWordBridge.start`: `armWakeWord()` calls `start(0.72)` when the "Hey Zynk" toggle is on and the models are ready, on toggle change, on `visibilitychange`, and 5 s after in-app dictation or web TTS ends. Since 2026-09-07 there is no in-app wake handler; every trigger is handled natively.

**`WakeWordService.onStartCommand`.** Reads `threshold` (default 0.5) and `modelDir`. Calls `startForeground` once per service life (type `MICROPHONE` on Android 14+, `DATA_SYNC` on 10 to 13; a `SecurityException` from a background start stops the service). Then a hard gate: if `NativeVoiceAnswerer.speaking`, `ZynkAssistantService.sessionActive` or `pausedForOtherRecording`, the start is deferred (the model dir is remembered, nothing else happens). Otherwise any running audio thread is stopped and joined (ONNX sessions are not safe for concurrent inference), the Vosk model is pre-loaded into `sharedVoskModel` on a thread if not already, and `loadAndStart(modelDir)` runs on a thread. ONNX sessions (`melSession`, `embSession`, `kwsSession`, one `OrtEnvironment`) are created once and kept across restarts; `stop()` (called from `onDestroy`) closes them.

**Audio loop (`startAudioLoop`, `processChunk`).** `AudioRecord(MIC, 16000, mono, PCM16)` with a buffer of at least `1280 * 2 * 8` bytes. The thread reads `CHUNK_SAMPLES = 1280` samples (80 ms) at a time. Each chunk is appended to `recentChunks` (ring of `TRIGGER_CLIP_CHUNKS = 40`, 3.2 s). If `cooldownRemaining > 0` the chunk is only counted down. Otherwise: samples scaled to float, mel model (`[1,1280]` in, 5 frames x 32 bins out) appended to `melBuffer` (ring of `MEL_WINDOW = 76` frames); when full, embedding model (`[1,76,32,1]` in, 96 floats out) appended to `embBuffer` (ring of `EMB_WINDOW = 16`); when full, classifier (`[1,16,96]` in, one probability out). The mel output is deliberately not normalised with openWakeWord's `mel/10 + 2`, because `hey_zynk.onnx` was trained without it (comment in code; do not add it without retraining).

**Decision.** `needHits` is 2 (4 in strict mode) consecutive chunks with score above `threshold` (0.90 in strict mode, `STRICT_SCORE`). On the deciding chunk: (a) silence gate: `recentLevelDb()` (RMS of the 3.2 s ring in dBFS) below `SILENCE_GATE_DB = -46.0` (same value for `STRICT_GATE_DB`) is ignored with a half cooldown; (b) verifier: `WakeVerifier.load` reads `assets/wake-word-models/hey_zynk_verifier.json` once; `score(flatEmb, 16, 96)` builds 16x96 + per-dimension mean + per-dimension max (1728 features), standardises with `mean`/`scale`, applies `coef`/`intercept`, sigmoid. With `VERIFIER_ENFORCE = true` a score below the file's `threshold` (0.5 in the shipped file, "v2, 33 real vs 60 false") is ignored, but the clip is still saved. (c) Accepted: `saveTriggerClip`, `cooldownRemaining = COOLDOWN_CHUNKS = 50` (about 4 s), `embBuffer.clear()`, `handleScreenOffDetection()`.

**Back-off.** `reportOutcome(useful)` is called by the session and answerer when a trigger ends. `noteOutcome` labels the newest clip (section 7) and, for a miss, records the time in `recentMisses`; three misses within `MISS_WINDOW_MS` (5 min) set `strictUntil = now + BACK_OFF_MS` (10 min). A useful outcome clears the misses and leaves strict mode. `isStrict()` is read by the session for the shape test.

**Hand-off (`handleScreenOffDetection`).** The name is historical; it is the single path for every trigger. It releases the audio-loop wake lock, acquires a partial wake lock `zynkbot:screen_off_wake` for 25 s, sets `running = false`, waits up to 2 s for `audioReleased` (the loop thread stops and releases `AudioRecord`), plays `R.raw.wake_chime` through `MediaPlayer` with `USAGE_MEDIA` (the assistant usage has no volume slider), then: if `ZynkAssistantService.instance` is non-null and `triggerSession()` (`showSession(Bundle(), 0)`) succeeds, extends the wake lock to 90 s and returns. Otherwise it falls back to `startKotlinVoskDictation()` inside the service (Vosk with 1.5 s silence stop and `MAX_LISTEN_MS = 12 s`), then `answerNatively(transcript)`: word gate (fewer than 2 or more than `MAX_QUERY_WORDS = 60` words is rejected with a closing tone), `VoiceCommands`, then `NativeVoiceAnswerer.answer`; if that returns false, `deliverTranscriptToApp` posts a tap-to-open notification (channel `wake_word_transcript_channel`, `PendingIntent` with `FLAG_CANCEL_CURRENT`) and, on non-GrapheneOS with the screen on, also tries `startActivity(MainActivity)`, which lands in `__handleScreenOffTranscript` (section 4).

**`ZynkAssistantSession` (the normal route).** `ZynkAssistantSessionService.onNewSession` returns a new session. `onShow`: `sessionActive = true`, `current = this`, `wakeScreen()` (a `SCREEN_BRIGHT_WAKE_LOCK | ACQUIRE_CAUSES_WAKEUP | ON_AFTER_RELEASE` lock, `zynkbot:assistant_session`, `SCREEN_LOCK_MS = 90 s`, because the session window alone does not light a dark screen), `setKeepAwake(true)`, show the Z overlay in `LISTENING` mode, `startListening()`. The overlay (`ZView`, `LOGO_DP = 120`, `BOTTOM_MARGIN_DP = 140`) is a three-stroke Z in `0xFF50FA7B` that draws in over 450 ms, breathes while listening and runs a travelling pulse while thinking; `onComputeInsets` makes only the Z's own rectangle touchable so taps elsewhere pass through; a tap calls `cancelByUser()` (report miss, stop listening and speech, close tone, hide).

Dictation: `startListening` reads `MainActivity.voiceInputSource(context)`; `"openai"` with an `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env` uses `startOpenAiListening`, else `startVoskListening`. Both first call `WakeWordService.instance?.releaseMicForSession()` on a background thread (blocks up to 2 s until `audioReleased`), because two readers on the mic wedged the session on the OnePlus. Vosk: `Recognizer(sharedVoskModel, 16000)`, `SpeechService`; three timers on the main looper: `silenceStop` re-armed `SILENCE_MS = 1500` after each partial, `noSpeechStop` at `NO_SPEECH_MS = 6000` if no partial ever arrives, `hardStop` at `SAFETY_TIMEOUT_MS = 12000` regardless. `stopVoskAsync` always stops Vosk off the main thread (its `stop()` joins a thread). OpenAI: `OpenAiDictation.record`, backstop `OPENAI_BACKSTOP_MS = 12000 + 20000 + 5000`; a `null` result that was not a cancel falls back to Vosk once (`onOpenAiDone`).

`answerAndFinish(transcript)`: word gate (2 to 60 words, else `reportOutcome(false)`, close tone, hide); in strict mode, `looksAddressedToAssistant` (a question mark, or one of a list of interrogative and imperative markers anywhere in the text) must pass unless it is a clock command, else it is closed as a miss without an API call; `VoiceCommands.parse` handles timer, alarm and stopwatch locally (`execute` uses `EXTRA_SKIP_UI = true`, returns true only if the clock app accepted the intent; `reportOutcome(true)`; the confirmation or `FAILED_LINE` is spoken by `NativeVoiceAnswerer.say`); otherwise the Z switches to `THINKING`, the close tone plays as a "sent" signal, and `NativeVoiceAnswerer.answer(context, transcript)` runs; `hide()` follows either way. `onHide`: `sessionActive = false`, release the screen lock, stop listening, stop the animation, and re-arm the wake word natively via `WakeWordService.instance?.resumeMicAfterSession()` (refused while speech is still playing; the answerer re-arms afterwards).

**`NativeVoiceAnswerer.answer`.** Sets `speaking = true`, notifies `onSpeakingChanged` (so the app's Stop button lights), calls `releaseMicForSession(500)` in case the recording watch had already re-armed the loop, then `answerInner`: get the process-wide `TextToSpeech` (lazy, `Locale.US`, `pickBestVoice` prefers the highest-quality installed English voice, offline over network), create a `SentenceSpeaker`, and call `ZynkCore.nativeSendMessage(transcript, "", "", "", "guardian", callback)`. Empty `userId`, `sessionId` and `backend` mean "resolve in Rust". The Rust side (`android_jni.rs`, `Java_ai_containai_zynkbot_ZynkCore_nativeSendMessage`) takes a global ref to the callback, resolves identity via `user_identity::get_identity()`, the session via `get_current_session_id()` (or creates `voice-<uuid>` and persists it), emits a `voice-session` event with the id, picks the backend with `resolve_voice_backend()` (`ZYNK_MODEL_BACKEND` if its credentials exist, else Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Mistral, custom, else an error), loads up to 40 recent turns (`load_recent_turns`), appends `HANDS_FREE_NOTE` to the model-facing message (the clean transcript still travels as `user_query`), and runs `commands::chat::generate_reply(..., hands_free = true)` on a process-wide tokio runtime with a `JniSink` that implements `ResponseSink` and forwards `onToken`, `onEvent`, `onDone(replyJson)`, `onError`.

`SentenceSpeaker.feed` buffers tokens and speaks each completed sentence (terminator followed by whitespace, at least 12 characters in) with `engine.speak(text, QUEUE_FLUSH for the first, QUEUE_ADD after, null, id)`; `MEMORY_EXTRACT` and `WEB_SEARCH_NEEDED` markers cut the stream; `cleanForSpeech` strips markdown and reads symbols as words. `onDone` parses `reply_text`: a reply starting with `NO_QUERY` is discarded silently and reported as a miss; otherwise a `Turn(sessionId, question, answer, at)` is added to `pendingTurns` and `onTurnCompleted` nudges the page (`window.__nativeTurns`), which drains `WakeWordBridge.drainNativeTurns()` and appends the turn to the chat when the thread on screen matches (`App.jsx`, `nativeTurnsToMessages`); the page drains again on `visibilitychange` because a nudge to a paused WebView is lost. `finish` speaks any remainder and waits up to 60 s for the utterances to settle (`onDone`, `onError`, and `onStop` all settle, so Stop does not leave the wake word deaf). A failure speaks `ERROR_LINE` and returns false. `finally`: `speaking = false`, notify, `resumeMicAfterSession()`.

The chimes are explicitly on `USAGE_MEDIA`. TTS itself is called with null params, so it plays on the engine's default stream. (An earlier internal note called this "TTS on the media stream"; the code sets no audio attributes on the engine, so it inherits the platform default.)

**Recording watch and mic hand-back.** `registerRecordingWatch` (in `onCreate`) registers an `AudioManager.AudioRecordingCallback`. `onRecordingsChanged` treats any active recording whose `clientAudioSessionId` differs from the loop's own (`loopSessionId`) as "someone else": another app, or Zynkbot's own Vosk or OpenAI dictation. While one exists, `pausedForOtherRecording = true` and the loop is stopped; when the last one ends, `resumeMicAfterSession()` restarts it. `resumeMicAfterSession` refuses while speaking, while another recording is active, or while a session is active, and restarts with a full cooldown so the tail of a reply cannot re-trigger.

**Wake locks.** `zynkbot:audio_loop` (partial) is acquired on `ACTION_SCREEN_OFF` and released on `ACTION_SCREEN_ON` so the ONNX loop keeps running with the screen dark; `zynkbot:screen_off_wake` (partial, 25 s then 90 s) covers one trigger; `zynkbot:assistant_session` (screen bright) lights the screen for the session, up to 90 s.

## 7. Trigger clips and labels

`WakeWordService.saveTriggerClip(score)` runs on every accepted detection and every verifier rejection. It snapshots `recentChunks` and `recentScores` and writes, off the audio thread, to `files/zynkbot/wake_triggers/`:

- `<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>-<score to 3 decimals>.wav`: 16 kHz mono PCM16, canonical 44-byte RIFF header (`wavHeader`), the last 40 chunks (3.2 s) ending with the chunk that fired.
- `<same stem>.scores.txt`: the classifier score for each of those chunks, four decimals, one per line, oldest first.

Retention: after each save, WAV files are sorted by name (newest first) and everything beyond `TRIGGER_CLIPS_KEPT = 20` is deleted along with its `.scores.txt`.

Labels: `labelLastClip(real)` writes `<stem>.real` (content `real`) or `<stem>.false` (content `false`) next to the newest clip when `reportOutcome` is called. In the code today `reportOutcome(true)` is called only from the clock-command path in `ZynkAssistantSession.answerAndFinish`; the model-answer path deliberately does not report success (comment in `NativeVoiceAnswerer.onDone`), and `NO_QUERY`, empty transcripts, strict-mode rejections and a tap on the Z report false. The comment in `NativeVoiceAnswerer.onDone` used to say explicit Remember also reported a real interaction; no code path does, and the comment was corrected on 2026-09-09. The retention pass now deletes a clip's `.scores.txt`, `.real` and `.false` sidecars with it (same date).

Training is a desktop script, not in the app: `WakeVerifier.kt` says the verifier is "trained on the desktop from this user's own clips against every false-trigger clip collected" and shipped as `hey_zynk_verifier.json` (`version`, `trained`, `threshold`, `mean`, `scale`, `coef`, `intercept`). Clips are pulled from a debug build with `adb shell run-as ai.containai.zynkbot` (comment in `saveTriggerClip`). The trainer is `labs/wake_verifier/train.py` (added to the repository 2026-09-09; sklearn logistic regression, C=0.05, class-balanced, standardised features, 5-fold cross-validation). It takes the model directory and a clips directory and writes `hey_zynk_verifier.json`; the `owners` list of device ids is added by hand. The clips themselves are not in the repository: they are Matt's voice and stay under `~/Documents/Zynk_related/wake_verifier_clips/`.

## 8. Dictation engines

There are three dictation paths on Android and one selector.

**Selector.** The Voice settings choice is stored in `localStorage` as `zynkbot_voice_input_source` (`'vosk'` default or `'openai'`). `useVoiceSession.setVoiceInputSource` also calls `AndroidPaths.setVoiceInputSource(val)`, and the same value is pushed again just before arming the wake word, so a stale native copy is corrected. Kotlin stores it in SharedPreferences `zynkbot_voice`, key `input_source`, and `MainActivity.voiceInputSource(context)` reads it for the native session. `EnvFile.read(context, "OPENAI_API_KEY")` decides whether the OpenAI choice is usable natively.

**Mic button in the app (`useVoiceInput.js`).** `isAndroid()` is `!!window.VoskBridge`. With `'vosk'`, `VoskBridge.startListening()` / `stopListening()` and the `__voskResult` callback. With `'openai'`, the WebView's own `getUserMedia` (the Android WebView is Chromium) captures audio in the page and the Rust `transcribe_audio` command uploads it; the Rust `start_vosk_recording` / `start_openai_recording` commands return an error on Android by `#[cfg(target_os = "android")]` (`lib.rs`), because `vosk_desktop.rs` (cpal + the `vosk` crate) exists only to work around the Linux WebKitGTK WebView's missing `getUserMedia` and is compiled only for Linux and Windows (`Cargo.toml` target sections, `mod vosk_desktop` in `lib.rs`).

**Vosk in the session.** `ZynkAssistantSession.startVoskListening` uses `WakeWordService.sharedVoskModel`, which is loaded either by `VoskBridge.startListening` or pre-loaded by `WakeWordService.onStartCommand`. If neither has run, the session hides with a log line. The model is the bundled `assets/vosk-model` ("US English model for mobile Vosk applications", Alpha Cephei, per its README; 68 MB on disk), extracted to `files/vosk-model` at first launch.

**`OpenAiDictation`.** `record(context, onSpeechStarted, onDone)` runs on a thread named `OpenAiDictation`: `AudioRecord` at `SAMPLE_RATE = 16000`, chunks of `CHUNK_MS = 50`; an adaptive noise floor is tracked until speech starts; onset is `SPEECH_ONSET_CHUNKS = 2` consecutive chunks above `max(noiseFloor * ONSET_FLOOR_MULT (2.5), MIN_SPEECH_RMS (120))`; `PRE_ROLL_CHUNKS = 10` (500 ms) before onset are kept; no onset within `SPEECH_WAIT_MS = 8000` returns `""`; after onset, `TRAILING_SILENCE_MS = 1200` of quiet ends it; `MAX_TOTAL_MS = 12000` caps the recording. The PCM is wrapped as a WAV in memory (`toWav`) and POSTed as multipart to `https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions` with `model=whisper-1`, `language=en`, `response_format=json`, `HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS = 20000`, bearer key from `.env`. `onDone` gets the trimmed `text`, `""` for no speech, or `null` for failure or cancel (`Recorder.isCancelled` tells them apart; cancel disconnects an in-flight upload). The session falls back to Vosk on `null`-not-cancelled, once.

## 9. Rust on Android

`Cargo.toml` `[lib] name = "app_lib"`, `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`, so the Rust core is `libapp_lib.so`. The generated `Rust.kt` loads it (`System.loadLibrary("app_lib")`) and `ZynkCore`'s `init` loads it again (idempotent) so the JNI door works even if called first.

Two doors into one core:

1. The WebView. Tauri IPC (`Rust.kt ipc`) dispatches to the `#[tauri::command]` functions registered in `lib.rs run()`; chat goes through `commands::chat::generate_reply` with a `TauriSink`.
2. `ZynkCore.nativeSendMessage`, the `#[no_mangle] extern "system"` function in `android_jni.rs` (compiled only with `#[cfg(target_os = "android")]`, declared as `mod android_jni` in `lib.rs`). It calls the same `generate_reply` with a `JniSink`. It keeps one `tokio` multi-thread runtime for the life of the process in a `OnceCell`, because `generate_reply` spawns background memory work that needs a runtime handle.

`resolve_voice_backend()` in `android_jni.rs` is the Android-only backend chooser; it treats `local` as unusable because `llm::local_models::resolve_default_model_path()` always errors on Android (section 11).

Where output goes: `lib.rs` shadows `println!` and `eprintln!` crate-wide with macros that call `app_log::line` and `app_log::err_line` (`app_log.rs`). Each writes the line to the real stdout or stderr and appends a timestamped copy to a ring buffer of `CAPACITY = 800` lines; `commands/report.rs build_problem_report` reads it back through `app_log::recent` and `app_log::redact` for "Report a problem" (device string supplied by `AndroidPaths.getDeviceInfo`). On Android, the real stdout and stderr are redirected by `tao`'s `ndk_glue.rs` (`create()` in the `tao` crate, version 0.35.3 in `~/.cargo/registry`): both file descriptors are `dup2`'d into a pipe and a thread writes every line to logcat at Info level with tag `RustStdoutStderr`. So `adb logcat -s RustStdoutStderr` shows the Rust log; Kotlin tags are `WakeWordService`, `ZynkAssistantSession`, `ZynkAssistantService`, `NativeVoiceAnswerer`, `OpenAiDictation`, `WakeVerifier`, `VoiceCommands`, `MainActivityLifecycle`, `ZynkWeb` (page breadcrumbs), and `Tauri` (generated `Logger.kt`).

Startup in `lib.rs run().setup`: create `models/system` and `models/user` under the data dir; load `.env` from `get_app_data_dir()/.env` with `dotenv` (dev-path fallbacks otherwise); register the dialog, shell and opener plugins (opener uses Android intents); store the app handle; warm up BERT NER on a thread; on another thread `db::create_pool()` runs `sqlx::migrate!("./migrations")` (idempotent, tracked in `_sqlx_migrations`), then `conversation_history::ensure_tables`, `seed_system_memories`, `index_system_documentation`; then the HTTP server for ZynkSync and ZynkLink starts.

Android-specific Cargo settings: `openssl` with `vendored` and `jni = "0.21"` are `[target.'cfg(target_os = "android")'.dependencies]`; `llama-cpp-2` and `cpal` are excluded on Android; `vosk` is Linux and Windows only. `.cargo/config.toml` sets `-C target-feature=+fullfp16,+fp16` for `aarch64-linux-android` (needed by candle's gemm; ARMv8.2-A, roughly 2018+ phones). The dev profile raises `opt-level = 3` for `sqlx-core`, `sqlx-sqlite` and `libsqlite3-sys` because unoptimised debug builds made a hands-free answer take 14 s on the OnePlus. Files with `#[cfg(target_os = "android")]` branches: `android_jni.rs`, `commands/knowledge_base.rs`, `db.rs`, `lib.rs`, `llm/mod.rs`, `user_identity.rs`.

## 10. Building and signing

**Local (from `zynkbot_rust/CLAUDE.md`).** Android Studio's bundled JDK is required; the system Java 8 does not compile Gradle:

```
JAVA_HOME=~/android-studio/jbr npm run tauri android build -- --apk
```

Add `-- --debug` for a debug build (needed for `run-as` access to `files/`, per the `Cargo.toml` comment). The Tauri CLI regenerates the gitignored files (`tauri.properties` with `versionName`/`versionCode` derived from `tauri.conf.json`'s `version`, `tauri.build.gradle.kts`, `tauri.settings.gradle`, `assets/tauri.conf.json`), then runs Gradle. Gradle's `rust` plugin (`buildSrc/.../RustPlugin.kt`) defines product flavours `universal`, `arm64`, `arm`, `x86`, `x86_64` on an `abi` dimension, and each `rustBuild<Arch><Profile>` task (`BuildTask.kt`) calls back into the CLI with `npm run -- tauri android android-studio-script --target <triple> [--release]` to produce the `.so` for that ABI, which is merged into `jniLibs`. Gradle 8.14.3 (wrapper), Android Gradle Plugin 8.11.0, Kotlin 1.9.25. `compileSdk = 36`, `targetSdk = 36`, `minSdk = 26`.

The Tauri-generated `assets/tauri.conf.json` still says `minSdkVersion: 24` (Tauri's default); Gradle's `minSdk = 26` is what the APK is built with, so Android 8.0 is the effective floor.

**Signing.** `build.gradle.kts` reads `gen/android/keystore.properties` (`storeFile`, `storePassword`, `keyAlias`, `keyPassword`; template in `keystore.properties.template`) into the `release` signing config, and `check(ksFile != null)` fails configuration if the file is missing. The `debug` build type uses Gradle's default debug keystore, keeps JNI debug symbols (`jniLibs.keepDebugSymbols` for all four ABIs) and allows cleartext traffic (`usesCleartextTraffic` placeholder true; false in release). CLAUDE.md's recipe for signing an unsigned APK by hand:

```
~/Android/Sdk/build-tools/<version>/apksigner sign \
  --ks ~/.android/debug.keystore --ks-pass pass:android \
  --out /tmp/app-signed.apk <unsigned.apk>
```

With `keystore.properties` present (it is on the development machine) a release build is signed by Gradle with the release key, and the `check()` makes the file mandatory even for debug builds. The `apksigner` step is only needed for the `--debug --apk` builds used during testing, which Gradle leaves unsigned.

**CI (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, job `release-android`, on tags `v*`, after the desktop job).** Ubuntu; Temurin Java 17; Android SDK with `platforms;android-34`; `sdkmanager "ndk;30.0.15729638" "build-tools;36.0.0"`, `ANDROID_NDK_HOME` set and the NDK's `llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin` put on `PATH`; Node 20; Rust stable with only the `aarch64-linux-android` target; `libssl-dev perl`; the keystore is decoded from secret `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` into `$HOME/keystores/zynkbot-release.jks` and `keystore.properties` is written from `ANDROID_STORE_PASSWORD`, `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS`, `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD`; `npm ci`; then `./gradlew assembleArm64Release` in `gen/android`; the output `app/build/outputs/apk/arm64/release/app-arm64-release.apk` is uploaded to the GitHub release as `Zynkbot_<version>.apk`. The release APK is therefore arm64 only. A separate `android-check` job in `test.yml` does a `cargo ndk` check of the Rust crate for `aarch64` and `armv7` with NDK 27 on every push; it does not build an APK.

**This job cannot work as written (KI-034).** It calls `gradlew` directly and never runs `tauri android build`, but `settings.gradle` applies `tauri.settings.gradle` unconditionally and that file, `app/tauri.build.gradle.kts`, `app/tauri.properties` and `assets/tauri.conf.json` are gitignored and absent on a fresh checkout, so Gradle fails at configuration time. The job has never run: at `v0.9.5-beta1` (the last tagged release) both desktop jobs failed and `release-android` was skipped. Until it is fixed, the Android release artefact is the AAB built locally with `tauri android build`.

**16 KB page-size alignment.** Google Play requires 16 KB-aligned native libraries for apps targeting Android 15+ (this app targets 36). `docs/ROADMAP.md` records it done in build33 (2026-09-07): `vosk-android 0.3.75`, `onnxruntime-android 1.29.0` (both in `app/build.gradle.kts`), and NDK 30 for `libapp_lib.so`; all five arm64 libraries (`libapp_lib.so`, `libvosk.so`, `libonnxruntime.so`, `libonnxruntime4j_jni.so`, `libjnidispatch.so`) verified at `0x4000`. The repository sets no `-Wl,-z,max-page-size` flag, so `libapp_lib.so`'s alignment comes from the NDK's default linker settings, which is why CI pins NDK 30 (`~/Android/Sdk/ndk` here has 27.0.12077973 and 30.0.15729638). To verify a built APK:

```
unzip -o app.apk 'lib/arm64-v8a/*' -d /tmp/apk
llvm-readelf -l /tmp/apk/lib/arm64-v8a/*.so | grep -E 'LOAD|Align'   # every LOAD must show Align 0x4000
~/Android/Sdk/build-tools/36.0.0/zipalign -c -P 16 -v 4 app.apk          # checks the APK's own .so alignment
```

Both checks were run on build50 (`app-universal-debug-signed.apk`) on 2026-09-09: all five arm64 libraries report `Align 0x4000` and `zipalign -c -P 16` reports "Verification successful".

**Versions.** `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `package.json` and the generated `tauri.properties` all say `0.9.6-beta1` / `versionCode 9006` (bumped 2026-09-09). The CI release name uses the `tauri.conf.json` version.

## 11. Things that differ from desktop

- **No local GGUF models.** `llm/mod.rs` replaces `local_models` with a stub on Android whose every function returns `LLMError::APIError("Local models not supported on Android")`; `llama-cpp-2` is not a dependency on Android. The model list is API backends and Ollama/custom endpoints only, and `resolve_voice_backend` skips a stale `local` preference.
- **No Rust-side dictation.** `vosk_desktop.rs` and `cpal` are desktop only; Android uses `VoskBridge` (in-app) or the session's own Vosk / `OpenAiDictation` (hands-free); in-app Whisper uses WebView `getUserMedia` plus the `transcribe_audio` command.
- **No opening folders, files or URLs from Rust.** `commands/knowledge_base.rs` returns "not supported on Android" for the open-folder, open-file and open-URL commands; the page hides the KB "Open folder" button when `window.AndroidFolderPicker` exists (`KnowledgeBasePanel.jsx`) and uses `AndroidPaths.openUrl` for the issues link.
- **File access is by `content://` URI.** Picked files are read through `AndroidPaths.readFileBase64` / `readFileText` (`ContentResolver`), not `read_file_base64` / `read_text_file` in Rust (`App.jsx handleAttachFile`); the camera capture is the exception (a real path from the FileProvider temp file). Files enter the KB and ZynkbotShare by copy (section 1).
- **Identity file location.** Android keeps `.zynk_*` files under `files/zynkbot`; desktop keeps them under `dirs::config_dir()/Zynkbot`.
- **Input behaviour.** Enter sends on desktop; on Android (`window.AndroidPaths` present) Enter inserts a newline and the placeholder omits the Shift+Enter hint (`App.jsx`).
- **Voice output.** In-app TTS on desktop is web audio; the hands-free reply on Android is Android `TextToSpeech`, and the app's Stop button is wired to both (`useVoiceSession.stopTts`).
- **Background services.** `SyncForegroundService` runs from launch so ZynkSync/ZynkLink keep working; there is no equivalent on desktop.
- **Assistant role and wake word.** Desktop has no wake word; on Android it depends on the `VoiceInteractionService` registration, the `microphone` foreground service, and the assistant role prompt.
- **Local network permission.** Android 16 needs `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK` at runtime for ZynkSync pairing.
- **Bundled Vosk model.** The APK ships the model in assets and copies it out at first launch; desktop looks for it under `models/system/vosk` (`vosk_desktop::find_model_dir`).
